The packaged `patch.diff` adds unrelated `--cs-global-alias` support and does not touch `src/idl_parser.cpp`, so the trace below is grounded on the staged vulnerable source plus `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `default_crash_trace.txt` / `reproduction_report.json`, not on that patch artifact.

analysis_state.reason: Stage 01's saved MSan trace clearly reaches `known_attributes_[name] = false` in `Parser::DoParse()` and attributes the poisoned value to stack slot `name628` in that function's frame. But the exact staged source-grounded witness path `attribute"";ta` only lexes `attribute`, clears `attribute_`, lexes the zero-length string constant `""`, copies a valid empty string into local `name`, and then uses that key at line 3429. No project-side statement visible in the staged source explains how `attribute_` or `name` becomes uninitialized on this path, and `run_flags.json` disables runtime disambiguation, so the available artifacts do not close a source-grounded project-side CWE-457 chain.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42501973 (flatbuffers): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target parser_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42501973
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 16-byte witness `72 22 61 74 74 72 69 62 75 74 65 22 22 3b 74 61` makes `flatbuffers_parser_fuzzer` discard its first two bytes and pass the literal parser body `attribute"";ta` into `flatbuffers::Parser::Parse()`. `Parser::Next()` first tokenizes the prefix `attribute`, so `Parser::DoParse()` enters the user-defined `attribute` declaration branch. That branch issues a second `NEXT()`: at line 340 the lexer clears `attribute_`, then the quoted-name scan sees the zero-length string constant `""`, executes zero loop iterations, and returns `token_ = kTokenStringConstant` with `attribute_` still equal to the valid empty string. `DoParse()` line 3422 copies that empty string into local `name`, and line 3429 passes `name` into `known_attributes_[name] = false`, where the saved MemorySanitizer trace reports the first observed read in libc++ `std::__1::basic_string::size()` during `std::map::operator[]`. The same trace says the poisoned value was created by stack allocation of `name628` in `Parser::DoParse` at line 3286, but the staged project source on the witnessed path does not show any statement that leaves `attribute_` or `name` uninitialized; it only shows a valid empty-string path reaching the sink. With runtime disambiguation disabled and the packaged patch unrelated to this parser path, the sample remains source-unresolved rather than a closed project-side uninitialized-value trace.

source.description: First project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled parser body and materializes the identifier token `attribute`, which is the control state that selects the later `attribute` declaration branch.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` bytes are `72 22 61 74 74 72 69 62 75 74 65 22 22 3b 74 61`. `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` ignores the first two bytes and passes the remaining C string `attribute"";ta` to `Parser::Parse()`. During the first `NEXT()`, lines 509-510 materialize the leading bytes `attribute` as the current identifier token.

sink.description: Exact project call site that reaches the saved MSan report. Registering the parsed attribute name performs a `std::map<std::string, bool>::operator[]` lookup, and libc++ consumes `name` in `std::string::size()` while comparing it against existing keys.
sink.note: The saved stack is `std::__1::basic_string::size() -> std::map::operator[] -> flatbuffers::Parser::DoParse:3429 -> ParseRoot -> Parse -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`. This sink clearly consumes the local `name` from step 5, but the staged source does not reveal which project-side statement poisoned MSan's `name628` stack slot before this call.

root_cause.description: Exact project-side materialization site for the local `name` key later passed to `known_attributes_[name] = false`. On the witnessed path, this statement copies the current `attribute_` text after the zero-length string literal has been lexed.
root_cause.note: This is the only branch-local `name` object later used at line 3429, so it is the best exact source anchor matching MSan's `name628` symbol. But the staged source on this path shows `attribute_ == ""`, so line 3422 source-groundedly constructs a valid empty `std::string` rather than exposing a project-side uninitialized write. The remaining poisoned-stack-slot transition is unresolved under the saved artifacts.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is the exact project-side statement that materializes the sink key from attacker-controlled parser state. On the witnessed path it copies `attribute_ == ""`; that explains which logical string reaches the sink, not why MSan still reports poisoned bytes in stack slot `name628`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact 16-byte witness satisfies `size >= 3`. The harness discards the first two bytes, converts the remainder to the NUL-terminated string `attribute"";ta`, and calls `Parser::Parse()` on that body.

evidence_limitations: On the exact witnessed `attribute"";ta` path, the staged vulnerable source only shows `attribute_.clear()`, a zero-iteration scan of the empty string constant `""`, and `auto name = attribute_;`; those operations source-groundedly produce a valid empty `std::string`, not an explicit uninitialized object.

The saved MemorySanitizer origin narrows the poison only to stack allocation of `name628` in `Parser::DoParse` at line 3286. It does not identify the precise project-side statement that leaves that stack slot uninitialized before line 3429 consumes it.

A remaining explanation would require runtime or library/ABI details outside the staged project source, but `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 could not instrument the workspace to disambiguate that fact.
The packaged `patch.diff` and metadata `fixed_commit` are unrelated to `src/idl_parser.cpp`, so they do not provide fix-grounded evidence for this parser path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness strips the first two bytes from the exact 16-byte witness and passes the remaining literal `attribute"";ta` into `Parser::Parse()`.

The lexer materializes the leading identifier token `attribute`; then the `attribute` branch's second `NEXT()` clears `attribute_` and returns the zero-length string constant `""` with `attribute_` still empty.

DoParse copies that empty parsed name into local `std::string name` and immediately uses it as the key in `known_attributes_[name] = false`, which is the exact project sink frame in the saved MSan report.

MSan says the poisoned value was created by stack allocation of `name628` in `DoParse`, but the staged project source does not expose a statement on this witness path that actually leaves `name` or `attribute_` uninitialized, so the trace remains unresolved.

fine_trace.note: Source. During the first `NEXT()` on attacker string `attribute"";ta`, the lexer consumes the leading bytes `attribute`, stores them in `attribute_`, and marks the current token as an identifier.

The main declaration loop evaluates `IsIdent("attribute")` true for the current token, so control enters the user-defined `attribute` declaration branch and issues a second `NEXT()` to lex the attribute name.
At the start of the branch's second `Parser::Next()` call, the lexer clears the previous token text, so `attribute_` becomes the empty string before the quoted attribute name is scanned.

The same `NEXT()` call lexes the following witness bytes `""` as a string constant. Because the opening quote is immediately followed by the closing quote, the loop at lines 371-468 executes zero iterations, no `attribute_ += ...` runs, and the cleared `attribute_` from step 3 is preserved as `""` while `token_` becomes `kTokenStringConstant`.

This exact project-side statement materializes the sink key from the parsed attribute text. On the witnessed path it copies the empty string from step 4 into branch-local `name`; that closes the logical `name` value reaching the sink, but it does not source-groundedly explain MSan's claim that stack slot `name628` is poisoned.

Sink. After `EXPECT(kTokenStringConstant)` and `EXPECT(';')` accept the witness fragment `"";`, the parser looks up/inserts the same local `name` in `known_attributes_`, which already contains built-in keys from parser construction. libc++ compares that key against existing map entries and the first observed read is `std::__1::basic_string::size()` from this call site. This closes the exact project sink path, but the staged source still does not expose the missing transition from the valid empty string at step 5 to MSan's poisoned `name628` stack slot.

allocation_context.note: The saved MSan origin says `Uninitialized value was created by an allocation of 'name628' in the stack frame` of `Parser::DoParse` at line 3286. In the staged source that line is the function entry, so the artifact narrows the origin to a stack slot in this frame but not to a precise project-side initialization failure.

format.name: 16-byte flatbuffers parser_fuzzer input
format.contract: The saved evidence proves only the exact 16-byte witness `72 22 61 74 74 72 69 62 75 74 65 22 22 3b 74 61`. In this witness the harness ignores the first two bytes and passes the exact literal `attribute"";ta` to `Parser::Parse()`. On the staged path, `DoParse` sees the keyword `attribute`, then the zero-length string constant `""`, then `;`, and finally uses local `name` as the key in `known_attributes_[name] = false`. The artifacts do not prove a broader class of empty attribute declarations because the project-side producer of MSan's poisoned `name628` stack slot remains unresolved.
